fieldsRead.text: This English-taught degree applies electricity and magnetism to physical devices and systems. Its core combines mathematics, circuits, electronics, signals, communication, fields, power and design projects, with applications in connected technology, healthcare and sustainable energy.

The UCR options offer related study in mathematical signals and systems, software, computational perception and motion, and renewable energy. The second adds more physical experimentation and energy/materials work. Substantial gaps remain in electronic devices, circuits, electromagnetic analysis, physical communications and electrical hardware; these are not equivalent electrical-engineering degrees.

Elective choices require approval and appropriate prior knowledge. The final project normally follows completion of 120 EC including all compulsory first-year courses. Specific project topics and future timetables depend on the programme.

This required 10-EC project runs over two consecutive quarters, normally quarters 3–4 of the third year. Entry requires 120 EC including all compulsory first-year courses. An optional 5-EC extension uses elective space; starting in quarter 1 requires the academic advisor’s permission.
One 10-EC programming and engineering-challenge unit spans the first two quarters; it is counted once.

Entry requires completion of the earlier offered course components containing communication, collaboration, planning and organising competences. These competences are embedded in the core and add no separate credits.

The full elective programme totals 45 EC across years 2–3, with at least 30 EC at intermediate/advanced level including 15 EC at advanced level. No content overlap is allowed. Submit for examination-board approval after earning 90 EC and obtain approval before final-project registration.
Thirty EC of the total 45-EC elective space is scheduled in year 3. The same level, non-overlap, prior-knowledge and approval rules apply; no fixed elective package is assumed.

Completion also requires at least five approved Studium Generale activities and MyFuture activities with total value seven. These do not add credits. The normal first-year study-advice threshold is 45 of 60 EC, subject to the applicable personal-circumstance rules.

The UCR programmes develop signal and system methods, computational perception and motion, software and renewable-energy analysis. The second places more weight on physical experiments, energy assessment and circular materials. Neither reproduces TU/e’s circuits, electronic devices, electromagnetic fields, physical communication systems, power hardware, instrumentation or electrical-engineering project sequence.

Combine linear-system and signal-processing methods with mathematical modelling, programming, software construction, algorithms, image-based perception and robotics. Physical foundations and renewable-energy conversion, storage and grid integration connect these methods to energy systems. Product-development work adds design, prototyping and performance trade-offs. This related-field programme has substantial gaps in circuits, electronic devices, electromagnetics and electrical hardware design.

Retain mathematical systems, programming, software, image-based perception and robotics while placing more weight on physical energy conversion, renewable-system assessment, materials and circular technology. Wave and materials experiments, energy-use analysis and solar-panel or electronic-waste recovery provide concrete technical methods. This direction does not provide the full electrical power, machines or electronics curriculum.
